properties.name: THE SWEEP'S ANSWER: only 5 of 191 open defect-facts were fixed-but-unclosed — the backlog is REAL, not bookkeeping residue, and option (d)'s premise is FALSE at scale
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-28 over the committed export, answering the question dec:idea-what-makes-a-field-report-owed named as the one that must be settled BEFORE choosing a remedy: 'How many of the 189 are actually live?'

THE ANSWER: almost all of them. 192 TemporalFacts carry fact_type=defect; 191 had no inbound INVALIDATES at sweep start. A text scan found fix-language anywhere in 28 of the 191. Reading those 28 in context rather than trusting the keyword — the discipline fact:a-findings-name-can-claim-more-than-its-data demands — only about 10 declare THEIR OWN closure, and only 5 had a ChangeEvent recording the work that did it. Those 5 are now closed with edges: bl-105, bl-217, the lost identity sidecar, set_verification_status erasing last_run_at, and the gate crashing on a directory artifact.

⭐⭐ SO OPTION (d) IS REFUTED AS A REMEDY, THOUGH IT WAS RIGHT AS A FIRST MOVE. Its premise was 'much of the 189 is surely fixed with nobody having drawn the edge'. That was true for 5 of 191 — 2.6%. Sweeping does NOT leave a backlog small enough to read without machinery, and any debt class designed on the assumption that the raw count is inflated by bookkeeping would be designed against a number that is very nearly the real one.

⭐ THE SECOND FINDING, AND IT EXPLAINS THE 8-EDGE TOTAL: THE CLOSURE CONVENTION HAS BEEN PROSE INSIDE THE FACT, NOT AN EDGE. The closed records were REWRITTEN in place — they open 'CLOSED 2026-08-07, same day, by...' or 'FIXED 2026-08-09.' and several then carry '--- ORIGINAL RECORD FOLLOWS ---'. A human reading the fact knows it is closed; no computation does. So the loop was not failing to record closures. It was recording them somewhere nothing can read, which is the same shape as fact:the-upstream-watch-is-findable-only-in-reflow2s-own-words.

⚠️ TWO CLASSES THE SWEEP COULD NOT CLOSE, AND BOTH ARE HONEST REFUSALS RATHER THAN OMISSIONS:
- FIXED ON MAIN, NOT YET RELEASED (fact:defect-create-node-merge-versus-replace-is-fixed-but-unreleased, fact:defect-loop-status-next-routes-to-the-destructive-skill). The code is right and every consumer still hits the bug. Closing these would tell a user running a release that their live defect is stale. Left open deliberately; this is a judgement for Anthony, not a bookkeeping call.
- SELF-CORRECTED IN PLACE, NOTHING TO POINT FROM (fact:defect-documented-hook-path-may-not-exist, fact:defect-set-artifact-checksums-accepts-a-malformed-digest). Both were MISDIAGNOSES — the reported harm does not occur — corrected by measurement written into the same node. There is no ChangeEvent because no code changed, and minting a node purely to host an edge would be bureaucracy. The convention has no answer for a finding that was simply wrong.

⭐ AND THE RECORDS ARE MORE DISCIPLINED THAN THE RAW COUNT SUGGESTS. At least six say plainly why they stay open: 'Left OPEN rather than closed, because only half of it moved'; 'Closing it here would report a class as fixed on the evidence of one case'; 'NOT FIXED HERE, and deliberately'. Nobody has been letting fixed things rot on the list. The list is long because the work is genuinely undone.

⚠️ WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: whether the ~181 still-open items are individually still true. This sweep measured which records CLAIM their own closure, not which defects a fresh test would still reproduce. Establishing that means re-running each against current code, which nobody has done and which this fact must not be read as having done.
